source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:7 (Tikkun Sefer Torah note declined; 'a Masorah in our hands: plene of plene, one of FIVE written with two yods — two of them in the Torah')
claim_en: היניקה ('she NURSED children — Sarah!') — PLENE OF PLENE, written with BOTH yods: one of the Masorah's five double-yod nursing-forms, two of them in the Torah. SNAPSHOT: both yods stand; the Torah twin is the nursing camels of Jacob's gift (מיניקות, 'nursing ones,' Gen 32:16) — the wonder-nursing and the caravan-nursing carry the same full spelling.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:7 (the same five-list, census leg)
claim_en: ...and the form היניקה itself is UNIQUE in the Torah — one token, Sarah's verse alone.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 21:7 (מלל two in two senses; and the gematria: מלל = one hundred — 'when Abraham was a HUNDRED, Sarah nursed children')
claim_en: מלל ('who would have SPOKEN to Abraham') — the rare speak-word is UNIQUE in the Torah: one token, this verse; the Masorah's second leg is the watchman's 'what of the night' oracle (Isa 21:11-12; edge) — 'Aram's fall comes in Abraham's merit.' And the Kitzur's arithmetic rides the letters: מ (40) + ל (30) + ל (30) = ONE HUNDRED, the father's age at the nursing (21:5 stands one verse before).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 21:10 (גרש three in the Masorah: 'drive out the maid' / 'drive out the scoffer' / 'he shall surely drive out' — 'because Sarah drove Hagar from her house... her children were driven out')
claim_en: THE MEASURE-FOR-MEASURE POINTING: consonantal גרש stands FIVE times in the Torah — but the drive-out imperative pointing (גָּרֵשׁ) exactly TWICE: Sarah's 'DRIVE OUT this maid' (21:10) and Pharaoh's expulsion of her children ('he shall surely DRIVE OUT,' Exod 11:1); the other three are a participle (Exod 34:11) and two nouns — one of them 'crushed grain' with a different final letter (Lev 2:14, Deut 33:14). The Masorah's third leg is 'drive out the scoffer' (Prov 22:10; edge). The Kitzur's moral — the driving-out returned on the driver's children — lives in a two-token pointing lock.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 21:10 (the pointing lock, letter-exact leg)
claim_en: ...and the two drive-out tokens are LETTER-IDENTICAL down to the accent: both גָּרֵ֛שׁ under tevir (the 'broken' accent) — Sarah's demand and the Egypt-payback carry one written form.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 21:15 (ויכלו three in the Masorah — 'my days are SPENT without hope'; 'spent in shame': 'for death by thirst is exceedingly shameful')
claim_en: ויכלו ('and the water was SPENT from the skin') — the consonants stand exactly TWICE in the Torah, and the pair preaches by pointing: creation's completed heavens (וַיְכֻלּוּ 'and they were FINISHED,' Gen 2:1 — the passive stem, dotted lamed) against the wilderness skin run dry (וַיִּכְלוּ, the plain stem) — fullness finished versus supply failed, split by one dot. The Masorah's other legs are Job's hopeless days (Job 7:6) and the accusers' shame (Ps 71:13; edges).

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 21:29 (הצבת two in the Masorah — 'in Abraham's merit all the bounds of earth were created')
claim_en: הצבת ('these seven ewes which you have SET apart') — UNIQUE in the Torah: one token, Avimelech's question at the well; the Masorah's pair-leg is 'You have SET all the bounds of the earth' (Ps 74:17; edge) — the ewes set apart at Beer Sheva answered by the world's set borders.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:18 ('the gimel is DAGESHED')
claim_en: גדול ('for a GREAT nation I will make him') — the gimel carries dagesh (the doubling dot), exactly as ruled: the greatness-word over Ishmael written with the pressed letter. SNAPSHOT: the dot stands.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:14 ('with PATACH on the mem'; the Shorashim cited)
claim_en: וחמת ('and a SKIN of water') — the mem pointed with patach (the open a-vowel), as Minchat Shai rules from the Shorashim. SNAPSHOT exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:14 ('ויתן אל הגר — with ONE telisha, on the heh alone')
claim_en: ויתן אל הגר ('and he GAVE to Hagar') — ONE telisha (the prepositive ornament-accent) in the phrase, standing on the heh of הגר ('Hagar') alone, exactly as ruled against the editions that double it. SNAPSHOT: one ornament, her name carries it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:16 (the Ramah: 'both plene... and EVERY death-word and every you-shall-die in the Torah likewise plene; and likewise in this phrase')
claim_en: במות ('let me not look on the DEATH of the child') — PLENE with vav, per the Ramah's whole-Torah rule: the death-word is always written full. SNAPSHOT: the vav stands in Hagar's cry.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:16 (the Ramah's proof-pair: Eden's sentence)
claim_en: ...and the Ramah's proof-pair stands at Eden's own sentence: מות ('you shall surely DIE,' Gen 2:17) — plene...

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:16 (the Ramah's proof-pair, second word)
claim_en: ...תמות ('you shall surely die,' the doubled verb's second word) — plene likewise: the death-word full from the first sentence to Hagar's averted eyes.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:25 ('אבימלך — with ETNACHTA')
claim_en: אבימלך ('and Abraham REPROVED Avimelech') — the king's name carries the etnachta (the verse's mid-rest), as ruled: the reproof pauses on its target. SNAPSHOT exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:25 ('עבדי — the dalet is RAFEH')
claim_en: עבדי ('the SERVANTS of Avimelech seized the well') — the dalet soft, WITHOUT dagesh (no doubling dot), as ruled. SNAPSHOT: undotted.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:23 ('גרתה בה — in some books WITHOUT maqqef')
claim_en: גרתה ('the land where you have SOJOURNED') — SNAPSHOT stands with Minchat Shai's some-books camp: NO maqqef (the joining stroke) after the sojourn-word; it keeps its own accent. Machine-checked by column.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:33 ('most books TZERE... one precise manuscript SEGOL, with a Masorah note: unique')
claim_en: אשל ('and he planted a TAMARISK') — the codices split: most books point the aleph with tzere (the long e); ONE precise manuscript points SEGOL (the short e) and carries a 'unique' Masorah note; the Radak and Rav Paalim record the same dispute. SNAPSHOT sides with the PRECISE-MANUSCRIPT camp: segol. Variance filed — tradition's majority against the codex line the DB descends from.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:33 ('אל עולם — the aleph with TZERE')
claim_en: אל עולם ('the EVERLASTING God' — the Name proclaimed at the tamarisk) — the aleph of אל pointed tzere, as ruled. SNAPSHOT exact.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:6 (the Masorah: 'accented on the FIRST syllable — and none like it counted among them'; כל השמע יצחק לי)
claim_en: יצחק־לי ('everyone who hears will LAUGH for me') — the laugh-verb is the Masorah's UNIQUE first-syllable-accented יצחק: SNAPSHOT writes the stress-stroke on the FIRST syllable (under the yod), maqqef-joined to לי ('for me').

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:6 (the same ruling; the name three verses earlier for the split)
claim_en: ...and the verb ends in PATACH (יצחק 'he will laugh') where the boy's name ends in QAMATZ (יצחק, 21:3) — consonant-identical, vowel-split: the letter conjugates the child's name into everyone's laughter and marks the difference with one vowel and the moved stress.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:6 (the name-side of the split)
claim_en: ...the name-side verified: יצחק at his naming (21:3) closes with qamatz.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 21:6 (maqqef leg)
claim_en: ...the maqqef leg machine-checked by column: the laugh-verb is joined to לי ('for me').
